Kenney was criticized at times for his record on [historic preservation](/wiki/Historic_preservation "Historic preservation"). After a number of significant historic churches and other buildings were torn down in the face of increased development pressures during Kenney's first mayoral term, former mayor John Street criticized the loss of the city's historic resources and founded a preservationist Political Action Committee in response.[[39]](#cite_note-39) In 2021, Josh Lippert, a city inspector who served on the Historic Commission resigned from his post after he said he was pressured by the Kenney Administration to vote against the designation of the 12th Street Gym and the properties adjacent to it. Lippert described a "pattern of interference from the Mayor’s Office" in the historic preservation process.[[40]](#cite_note-40)

Main article: [1953 British Mount Everest expedition](/wiki/1953_British_Mount_Everest_expedition "1953 British Mount Everest expedition")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c1/Edmund_Hillary_and_Tenzing_Norgay.jpg/250px-Edmund_Hillary_and_Tenzing_Norgay.jpg)](/wiki/File:Edmund_Hillary_and_Tenzing_Norgay.jpg)

[Edmund Hillary](/wiki/Edmund_Hillary "Edmund Hillary") and [Tenzing Norgay](/wiki/Tenzing_Norgay "Tenzing Norgay")

In 1953, a ninth British expedition, led by [John Hunt](/wiki/John_Hunt,_Baron_Hunt "John Hunt, Baron Hunt"), returned to Nepal. Hunt selected two climbing pairs to attempt the summit. The first, [Tom Bourdillon](/wiki/Tom_Bourdillon "Tom Bourdillon") and [Charles Evans](/wiki/Charles_Evans_(mountaineer) "Charles Evans (mountaineer)"), came within 100 m (330 ft) of the summit on 26 May 1953, but turned back after running into oxygen problems. As planned, their work in routefinding, breaking trail and oxygen caches were of great aid to the following pair. Two days later, the expedition made its second assault with the second pair: New Zealander [Edmund Hillary](/wiki/Edmund_Hillary "Edmund Hillary") and [Tenzing Norgay](/wiki/Tenzing_Norgay "Tenzing Norgay"), a Nepali [Sherpa](/wiki/Sherpa_people "Sherpa people") climber. They reached the summit at 11:30 am local time on 29 May 1953 via the South Col route. At the time, both acknowledged it as a team effort by the whole expedition, but Tenzing revealed a few years later that Hillary had put his foot on the summit first.[[114]](#cite_note-Ullman-122) They took photos and buried sweets and a small cross in the snow before descending.[[115]](#cite_note-123)

Bad Bunny has set numerous records in both Latin and global music. In January 2025, with the release of *[Debí Tirar Más Fotos](/wiki/Deb%C3%AD_Tirar_M%C3%A1s_Fotos "Debí Tirar Más Fotos")*, he became the first Latin artist to surpass 100 entries on the [*Billboard* Hot 100](/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"), bringing his career total to 113 entries.[[233]](#cite_note-235) Of these entries, 41 reached the top 40, 12 reached the top 10, and one—"[I Like It](/wiki/I_Like_It_(Cardi_B,_Bad_Bunny_and_J_Balvin_song) "I Like It (Cardi B, Bad Bunny and J Balvin song)")" with [Cardi B](/wiki/Cardi_B "Cardi B") and [J Balvin](/wiki/J_Balvin "J Balvin")—reached number one.[[234]](#cite_note-billboard-100hits-236) He also holds the record for the most entries on the [Hot Latin Songs](/wiki/Hot_Latin_Songs "Hot Latin Songs") chart with 189 career entries.[[234]](#cite_note-billboard-100hits-236)

On [Spotify](/wiki/Spotify "Spotify"), Bad Bunny has been named the platform's most-streamed artist globally a record four times (2020, 2021, 2022, and 2025), making him the first and only artist to achieve this distinction.[[235]](#cite_note-237) In 2020, he became the first non-English language artist to top Spotify's year-end most-streamed list.[[236]](#cite_note-238) His 2025 total of 19.8 billion streams was driven largely by *Debí Tirar Más Fotos*, which was also named the most-streamed album globally that year.[[237]](#cite_note-239)

His album *[Un Verano Sin Ti](/wiki/Un_Verano_Sin_Ti "Un Verano Sin Ti")* became the [most-streamed album in Spotify history](/wiki/List_of_Spotify_streaming_records "List of Spotify streaming records")[[238]](#cite_note-240) and was the first Spanish-language album nominated for the [Grammy Award for Album of the Year](/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Album_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Album of the Year").[[239]](#cite_note-241)

It extends into neighboring southern [Iraq](/wiki/Iraq "Iraq"), southern [Jordan](/wiki/Jordan "Jordan"), central [Qatar](/wiki/Qatar "Qatar"), most of the [Abu Dhabi](/wiki/Abu_Dhabi "Abu Dhabi") emirate in the [United Arab Emirates](/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"), western [Oman](/wiki/Oman "Oman"), and northeastern [Yemen](/wiki/Yemen "Yemen"). The ecoregion also includes most of the [Sinai Peninsula](/wiki/Sinai_Peninsula "Sinai Peninsula") in [Egypt](/wiki/Egypt "Egypt") and the adjacent [Negev](/wiki/Negev "Negev") desert in southern Israel.[[1]](#cite_note-dopa-1)

The [Rub' al-Khali](/wiki/Rub%27_al-Khali "Rub' al-Khali") desert is a [sedimentary basin](/wiki/Sedimentary_basin "Sedimentary basin") stretching along a south-west to north-east axis across the Arabian Shelf.[[5]](#cite_note-5) At an altitude of 1,000 metres (3,300 ft), rock landscapes yield to the Rub' al-Khali, a vast stretch of sand whose extreme southern point crosses the center of Yemen. The sand overlies gravel or gypsum plains and the dunes reach maximum heights of up to 250 m (820 ft). The sands are predominantly silicates, composed of 80 to 90% quartz and the remainder feldspar, whose iron oxide-coated grains color the sands orange, purple, and red.
